title: DuckStation ports a luma-quantized scanline filter with independent grid control
summary: The Modern shader varies scanline strength across perceived brightness, exposes horizontal and vertical density separately, and includes channel attenuation for unusually bright source palettes.
heroAlt: Visual evidence from DuckStation pull request #3731: Modern Lossless Dynamic Quantization Scanline Shader

sourceLabels.duckstation-pr-3731: Modern Lossless Dynamic Quantization Scanline Shader

blocks.text: This filter targets scaling structure rather than literal CRT simulation

The shader is a port of the libretro scanlines-Modern implementation, but its stated goal is not simply to reproduce a cathode-ray tube. It tries to retain the sharpness of modern displays while adding a controllable grid that helps enlarged source pixels read consistently. Horizontal crosslines and vertical scanlines have separate strength and density controls, allowing the pattern to match output resolution instead of assuming one monitor geometry.
Dynamic quantization follows the image's perceived brightness

Rather than applying the same dark stripe to every pixel, the filter calculates intensity from a perceptual luma curve. Mid-tones receive the clearest scanline structure, while deep shadows and strong highlights weaken the effect. This avoids flattening the brightest and darkest areas merely to keep the grid uniform. The quantized response also gives the pattern discrete, stable steps instead of letting tiny luma changes constantly alter its strength.
Channel attenuation addresses gamma-biased source palettes

The shader exposes color-channel quantization attenuation for material whose original display assumptions produced an over-bright or washed appearance on a modern panel. The source mentions handheld-style gamma bias as a motivating case even though DuckStation emulates PlayStation. That control should be understood as an optional post-processing tool, not a correction DuckStation applies to game color by default.
A useful comparison varies both output resolution and image luma

Testing should cover 1080p and 4K output, integer and non-integer window scales, and scenes dominated by shadows, mid-tones, or highlights. Adjust vertical and horizontal density independently and inspect pixel fonts, gradients, transparency, and scrolling backgrounds. Record unfiltered color and histogram references so a vivid result is not mistaken for preservation. Performance should also be measured because a customizable filter may cost more than the fixed 4x2 variant.
Dynamic luma response and independent grid axes distinguish this filter from the fixed 4x2 preset; they solve a different tuning problem and are not duplicate news.
